sanskrit: samitir dharmarājasya sā pārthivasamākulā śuśubhe tārakācitrā dyauś candreṇeva bhārata
english: That assembly of the king of dharma, crowded with lords of the earth, shone resplendent — like the sky bright with stars and the moon, O Bharata.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca tathā vyūḍheṣv anīkeṣu kurukṣetre dvijarṣabha kim akurvanta kuravaḥ kālenābhipracoditāḥ
english: Janamejaya said: When the armies had thus been arrayed on the field of Kurukshetra, O bull among twice-born, what did the Kurus do, impelled by time?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathā vyūḍheṣv anīkeṣu yat teṣu bharatarṣabha dhṛtarāṣṭro mahārāja saṃjayaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Vaishampayana said: When those armies had thus been arrayed, O bull of the Bharatas, the great king Dhritarashtra spoke these words to Sanjaya.

sanskrit: ehi saṃjaya me sarvam ācakṣvānavaśeṣataḥ senāniveśe yadvṛttaṃ kurupāṇḍavasenayoḥ
english: "Come, Sanjaya — tell me everything without remainder: whatever has occurred at the camp among the armies of the Kurus and Pandavas."

sanskrit: diṣṭam eva paraṃ manye pauruṣaṃ cāpy anarthakam yad ahaṃ jānamāno 'pi yuddhadoṣān kṣayodayān
english: "I consider destiny supreme and human effort fruitless — for even though I know the evils of war and its ruinous consequences,"

sanskrit: tathāpi nikṛtiprajñaṃ putraṃ durdyūtadevinam na śaknomi niyantuṃ vā kartuṃ vā hitam ātmanaḥ
english: "Yet I cannot restrain my son, whose judgment is warped and who plays at wicked dice, nor can I act for my own welfare."

sanskrit: bhavaty eva hi me sūta buddhir doṣānudarśinī duryodhanaṃ samāsādya punaḥ sā parivartate
english: "Indeed, O Suta, a discernment of faults arises in me, but when it encounters Duryodhana, it turns back again."

sanskrit: evaṃ gate vai yad bhāvi tad bhaviṣyati saṃjaya kṣatradharmaḥ kila raṇe tanutyāgo 'bhipūjitaḥ
english: "Things being so, O Sanjaya, whatever is destined shall come to pass. The duty of a warrior, it is said, is revered as the laying down of the body in battle."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tvadyukto 'yam anupraśno mahārāja yathārhasi na tu duryodhane doṣam imam āsaktum arhasi śṛṇuṣvānavaśeṣeṇa vadato mama pārthiva
english: Sanjaya said: "This inquiry of yours is appropriate, O great king, as befits you. Yet you ought not to fix this blame on Duryodhana alone. Hear me fully as I speak, O lord of the earth."

sanskrit: ya ātmano duścaritād aśubhaṃ prāpnuyān naraḥ enasā na sa daivaṃ vā kālaṃ vā gantum arhati
english: "A man who incurs misfortune through his own misconduct ought not to lay that sin upon destiny or upon time."

sanskrit: mahārāja manuṣyeṣu nindyaṃ yaḥ sarvam ācaret sa vadhyaḥ sarvalokasya ninditāni samācaran
english: "O great king, a man who practices everything blameworthy among men, who commits what all the world condemns, deserves destruction by all the world."

sanskrit: nikārā manujaśreṣṭha pāṇḍavais tvatpratīkṣayā anubhūtāḥ sahāmātyair nikṛtair adhidevane
english: "O foremost of men, the Pandavas endured insults, waiting on you, deceived with their ministers through the crooked dice-play."

sanskrit: hayānāṃ ca gajānāṃ ca rājñāṃ cāmitatejasām vaiśasaṃ samare vṛttaṃ yat tan me śṛṇu sarvaśaḥ
english: "Hear from me in full what slaughter has occurred in battle — of horses, of elephants, and of kings of immeasurable splendor."

sanskrit: sthiro bhūtvā mahārāja sarvalokakṣayodayam yathābhūtaṃ mahāyuddhe śrutvā mā vimanā bhava
english: "Be steadfast, O great king, and having heard of the rise and fall of all the world as it truly occurred in this great war, do not become despondent."

sanskrit: na hy eva kartā puruṣaḥ karmaṇoḥ śubhapāpayoḥ asvatantro hi puruṣaḥ kāryate dāruyantravat
english: "For a person is not truly the author of good or evil actions; a person is not free — he is driven like a wooden puppet."

sanskrit: ke cid īśvaranirdiṣṭāḥ ke cid eva yadṛcchayā pūrvakarmabhir apy anye traidham etad vikṛṣyate
english: "Some are directed by the Lord, some by chance, and others by the actions of former lives — this threefold force pulls men apart."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca hiraṇvatyāṃ niviṣṭeṣu pāṇḍaveṣu mahātmasu duryodhano mahārāja karṇena saha bhārata
english: Sanjaya said: When the great-souled Pandavas had encamped on the Hiranvati, O great king, Duryodhana — together with Karna, O Bharata —

sanskrit: saubalena ca rājendra tathā duḥśāsanena ca āhūyopahvare rājann ulūkam idam abravīt
english: — and with Shakuni the son of Subala, O king of kings, and with Duhshasana — having summoned Uluka aside, O king, spoke thus:

sanskrit: ulūka gaccha kaitavya pāṇḍavān sahasomakān gatvā mama vaco brūhi vāsudevasya śṛṇvataḥ
english: "Go, Uluka, son of Shakuni — go to the Pandavas together with the Somakas, and speak my words in the hearing of Vasudeva."

sanskrit: idaṃ tat samanuprāptaṃ varṣapūgābhicintitam pāṇḍavānāṃ kurūṇāṃ ca yuddhaṃ lokabhayaṃkaram
english: "This war, terrible to all the world, which has been pondered over many years by the Pandavas and the Kurus alike, has now arrived."

sanskrit: yad etat katthanāvākyaṃ saṃjayo mahad abravīt madhye kurūṇāṃ kaunteya tasya kālo 'yam āgataḥ yathā vaḥ saṃpratijñātaṃ tat sarvaṃ kriyatām iti
english: "That great boast which Sanjaya spoke in the midst of the Kurus, O son of Kunti — the time for it has come. Let everything be done as you have pledged."

sanskrit: amarṣaṃ rājyaharaṇaṃ vanavāsaṃ ca pāṇḍava draupadyāś ca parikleśaṃ saṃsmaran puruṣo bhava
english: "Remember the wrath, O Pandava — the seizure of the kingdom, the forest exile, and the humiliation of Draupadi — and be a man!"

sanskrit: yadarthaṃ kṣatriyā sūte garbhaṃ tad idam āgatam balaṃ vīryaṃ ca śauryaṃ ca paraṃ cāpy astralāghavam pauruṣaṃ darśayan yuddhe kopasya kuru niṣkṛtim
english: "That for which a warrior woman bears a son in her womb has now arrived. Showing your strength, valor, heroism, and supreme skill with weapons in battle, make expiation for your wrath."

sanskrit: parikliṣṭasya dīnasya dīrghakāloṣitasya ca na sphuṭed dhṛdayaṃ kasya aiśvaryād bhraṃśitasya ca
english: "Whose heart would not burst — one who has been tormented, impoverished, who has lived long in hardship, and who has been stripped of sovereignty?"

sanskrit: kule jātasya śūrasya paravitteṣu gṛdhyataḥ ācchinnaṃ rājyam ākramya kopaṃ kasya na dīpayet
english: "Of a hero born in a noble house, whose kingdom was seized by one greedy for another's wealth — whose anger would not be kindled?"

sanskrit: yat tad uktaṃ mahad vākyaṃ karmaṇā tad vibhāvyatām akarmaṇā katthitena santaḥ kupuruṣaṃ viduḥ
english: "Let that great speech which was spoken be now demonstrated by deeds; the virtuous know that one who boasts but does not act is a base person."

sanskrit: amitrāṇāṃ vaśe sthānaṃ rājyasya ca punarbhavaḥ dvāv arthau yudhyamānasya tasmāt kuruta pauruṣam
english: "Two outcomes attend a warrior in battle: to remain under the power of enemies, or to recover the kingdom. Therefore, show your manhood!"

sanskrit: asmān vā tvaṃ parājitya praśādhi pṛthivīm imām atha vā nihato 'smābhir vīralokaṃ gamiṣyasi
english: "Either defeat us and rule this earth, or be slain by us and go to the world of heroes."

sanskrit: rāṣṭrāt pravrājanaṃ kleśaṃ vanavāsaṃ ca pāṇḍava kṛṣṇāyāś ca parikleśaṃ saṃsmaran puruṣo bhava
english: "Remember the banishment from the kingdom, the suffering, the forest exile, O Pandava, and the humiliation of Krishnaa — and be a man!"

sanskrit: apriyāṇāṃ ca vacane pravrajatsu punaḥ punaḥ amarṣaṃ darśayādya tvam amarṣo hy eva pauruṣam
english: "As unpleasant words were spoken and you went into exile again and again — show your indignation now, for indignation itself is manhood."

sanskrit: krodho balaṃ tathā vīryaṃ jñānayogo 'stralāghavam iha te pārtha dṛśyantāṃ saṃgrāme puruṣo bhava
english: "Let your wrath, strength, valor, mastery of knowledge, and lightness of hand with weapons be seen here in the battle, O Partha — be a man!"

sanskrit: taṃ ca tūbarakaṃ mūḍhaṃ bahvāśinam avidyakam ulūka madvaco brūyā asakṛd bhīmasenakam
english: "And to that glutton Bhimasena, O Uluka — that dullard, that ignorant braggart — repeat my words more than once:"

sanskrit: aśaktenaiva yac chaptaṃ sabhāmadhye vṛkodara duḥśāsanasya rudhiraṃ pīyatāṃ yadi śakyate
english: "'What was sworn in the assembly hall by one who was powerless, O wolf-belly — let the blood of Duhshasana be drunk, if it can be done!'"

sanskrit: lohābhihāro nirvṛttaḥ kurukṣetram akardamam puṣṭās te 'śvā bhṛtā yodhāḥ śvo yudhyasva sakeśavaḥ
english: "The supply of iron is ready, Kurukshetra is free of mud, your horses are well-fed, your warriors are paid — tomorrow fight together with Keshava!"

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca senāniveśaṃ saṃprāpya kaitavyaḥ pāṇḍavasya ha samāgataḥ pāṇḍaveyair yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata
english: Sanjaya said: Having reached the camp of the Pandavas, Uluka, son of Shakuni, was brought before Yudhishthira by the Pandava princes and addressed him.

sanskrit: abhijño dūtavākyānāṃ yathoktaṃ bruvato mama duryodhanasamādeśaṃ śrutvā na kroddhum arhasi
english: "Knowing the protocols of envoys and the words I speak as instructed, you should not grow angry upon hearing Duryodhana's commission."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ulūka na bhayaṃ te 'sti brūhi tvaṃ vigatajvaraḥ yan mataṃ dhārtarāṣṭrasya lubdhasyādīrghadarśinaḥ
english: Yudhishthira said: "Uluka, you have no cause for fear — speak without anxiety what is the view of the son of Dhritarashtra, that greedy man of short-sighted vision."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato dyutimatāṃ madhye pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām sṛñjayānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ kṛṣṇasya ca yaśasvinaḥ
english: Sanjaya said: Then, in the midst of the brilliant great-souled Pandavas, and of all the Srinjayas, and of the illustrious Krishna —

sanskrit: drupadasya saputrasya virāṭasya ca saṃnidhau bhūmipānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ madhye vākyaṃ jagāda ha
english: — in the presence of Drupada with his sons, and of Virata, and in the midst of all those lords of the earth, Uluka spoke the following words:

sanskrit: idaṃ tvām abravīd rājā dhārtarāṣṭro mahāmanāḥ śṛṇvatāṃ kuruvīrāṇāṃ tan nibodha narādhipa
english: "Thus spoke the great-minded king, son of Dhritarashtra, while the Kuru heroes listened. Understand this, O lord of men:"

sanskrit: parājito 'si dyūtena kṛṣṇā cānāyitā sabhām śakyo 'marṣo manuṣyeṇa kartuṃ puruṣamāninā
english: "'You were defeated at dice, and Krishnaa was dragged into the assembly hall. A man who considers himself a man ought to be able to feel indignation.'"

sanskrit: dvādaśaiva tu varṣāṇi vane dhiṣṇyād vivāsitāḥ saṃvatsaraṃ virāṭasya dāsyam āsthāya coṣitāḥ
english: "'You were exiled from your home for twelve full years in the forest, and lived as servants in Virata's court for one year.'"

sanskrit: amarṣaṃ rājyaharaṇaṃ vanavāsaṃ ca pāṇḍava draupadyāś ca parikleśaṃ saṃsmaran puruṣo bhava
english: "'Remember the wrath, the seizure of the kingdom, the forest exile, O Pandava, and the humiliation of Draupadi — and be a man!'"

sanskrit: aśaktena ca yac chaptaṃ bhīmasenena pāṇḍava duḥśāsanasya rudhiraṃ pīyatāṃ yadi śakyate
english: "'What was sworn by the powerless Bhimasena, O Pandava — let the blood of Duhshasana be drunk, if it can be done!'"

sanskrit: lohābhihāro nirvṛttaḥ kurukṣetram akardamam samaḥ panthā bhṛtā yodhāḥ śvo yudhyasva sakeśavaḥ
english: "'The supply of iron is ready, Kurukshetra is free of mud, the road is even, the warriors are paid — tomorrow fight together with Keshava!'"

sanskrit: asamāgamya bhīṣmeṇa saṃyuge kiṃ vikatthase ārurukṣur yathā mandaḥ parvataṃ gandhamādanam
english: "'Why do you boast without having encountered Bhishma in battle — like a fool wishing to climb Mount Gandhamadana?'"

sanskrit: droṇaṃ ca yudhyatāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ śacīpatisamaṃ yudhi ajitvā saṃyuge pārtha rājyaṃ katham ihecchasi
english: "'Without defeating Drona, the foremost of warriors, equal in battle to the lord of Shachi, how do you desire the kingdom here, O Partha?'"

sanskrit: brāhme dhanuṣi cācāryaṃ vedayor antaraṃ dvayoḥ yudhi dhuryam avikṣobhyam anīkadharam acyutam
english: "'The teacher who is supreme in the brahma-bow, who knows the distinction between the two Vedas, who bears the army unshaken and steadfast in battle, the unfailing one —'"

sanskrit: droṇaṃ mohād yudhā pārtha yaj jigīṣasi tan mṛṣā na hi śuśruma vātena merum unmathitaṃ girim
english: "'That you wish in delusion to conquer Drona in battle, O Partha — that is false. For we have never heard of Mount Meru being shaken by the wind.'"

sanskrit: anilo vā vahen meruṃ dyaur vāpi nipaten mahīm yugaṃ vā parivarteta yady evaṃ syād yathāttha mām
english: "'The wind might carry off Mount Meru, or the sky might fall upon the earth, or the age might be reversed — if what you say about me were true.'"

sanskrit: ko hy ābhyāṃ jīvitākāṅkṣī prāpyāstram arimardanam gajo vājī naro vāpi punaḥ svasti gṛhān vrajet
english: "'Who, wishing to live, having once received the weapons of those two foe-crushers — be it elephant, horse, or man — would return safely home again?'"

sanskrit: katham ābhyām abhidhyātaḥ saṃsṛṣṭo dāruṇena vā raṇe jīvan vimucyeta padā bhūmim upaspṛśan
english: "'How could one who is targeted by those two and who has come into contact with their terrible weapons escape alive from battle, even touching the earth with his feet?'"

sanskrit: kiṃ darduraḥ kūpaśayo yathemāṃ; na budhyase rājacamūṃ sametām durādharṣāṃ devacamūprakāśāṃ; guptāṃ narendrais tridaśair iva dyām
english: "'Are you like a frog dwelling in a well, that you do not perceive this royal army assembled — invincible, brilliant as the army of the gods, protected by lords of men like the sky by the thirty gods?'"

sanskrit: prācyaiḥ pratīcyair atha dākṣiṇātyair; udīcyakāmbojaśakaiḥ khaśaiś ca śālvaiḥ samatsyaiḥ kurumadhyadeśair; mlecchaiḥ pulindair draviḍāndhrakāñcyaiḥ
english: "'— With the easterners, the westerners, the southerners, the northerners, the Kambojas, the Shakas, the Khashas, the Shalvas, the Matsyas, the people of the Kuru midlands, the Mlechchhas, the Pulindas, the Dravidas, the Andhras, and the Kanchis —'"

sanskrit: nānājanaughaṃ yudhi saṃpravṛddhaṃ; gāṅgaṃ yathā vegam avāraṇīyam māṃ ca sthitaṃ nāgabalasya madhye; yuyutsase manda kim alpabuddhe
english: "'— the vast flood of diverse peoples swelling in battle, unstoppable as the current of the Ganga — and me standing in the midst of a force strong as elephants — do you wish to fight me, O dullard of little intelligence?'"

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā rājānaṃ dharmaputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram abhyāvṛtya punar jiṣṇum ulūkaḥ pratyabhāṣata
english: Having spoken thus to king Yudhishthira, the son of Dharma, Uluka turned and again addressed Arjuna, the victorious one:

sanskrit: akatthamāno yudhyasva katthase 'rjuna kiṃ bahu paryāyāt siddhir etasya naitat sidhyati katthanāt
english: "Fight without boasting — why do you boast so much, Arjuna? Success in this comes in due course; it is not achieved by boasting."

sanskrit: yadīdaṃ katthanāt sidhyet karma loke dhanaṃjaya sarve bhaveyuḥ siddhārthā bahu kattheta durgataḥ
english: "If deeds in the world were accomplished by boasting, O Dhananjaya, then every person in want could boast greatly and have all their aims fulfilled."

sanskrit: jānāmi te vāsudevaṃ sahāyaṃ; jānāmi te gāṇḍivaṃ tālamātram jānāmy etat tvādṛśo nāsti yoddhā; rājyaṃ ca te jānamāno harāmi
english: "I know you have Vasudeva as your ally; I know your bow Gandiva is as tall as a palm tree; I know all this — that there is no warrior like you — and yet knowing this, I take your kingdom."

sanskrit: na tu paryāyadharmeṇa siddhiṃ prāpnoti bhūyasīm manasaiva hi bhūtāni dhātā prakurute vaśe
english: "Yet one does not attain great success merely by the law of due course; for the Creator brings beings under his control through the mind alone."

sanskrit: trayodaśa samā bhuktaṃ rājyaṃ vilapatas tava bhūyaś caiva praśāsiṣye nihatya tvāṃ sabāndhavam
english: "For thirteen years I enjoyed the kingdom while you lamented; I shall rule it again after slaying you along with your kinsmen."

sanskrit: kva tadā gāṇḍivaṃ te 'bhūd yat tvaṃ dāsapaṇe jitaḥ kva tadā bhīmasenasya balam āsīc ca phalguna
english: "Where was your Gandiva then when you were staked and lost as a slave? Where was the strength of Bhimasena then, O Phalguna?"

sanskrit: sagadād bhīmasenāc ca pārthāc caiva sagāṇḍivāt na vai mokṣas tadā vo 'bhūd vinā kṛṣṇām aninditām
english: "From Bhimasena with his mace and from Partha with his Gandiva — there was no deliverance for you at that time without the blameless Krishnaa."

sanskrit: sā vo dāsyaṃ samāpannān mokṣayām āsa bhāminī amānuṣyasamāyuktān dāsyakarmaṇy avasthitān
english: "That noble lady rescued you when you had fallen into slavery, you who were caught in inhuman conditions and reduced to servitude."

sanskrit: avocaṃ yat ṣaṇḍhatilān ahaṃ vas tathyam eva tat dhṛtā hi veṇī pārthena virāṭanagare tadā
english: "What I called you — sesame seeds without kernel — that was the very truth; for Partha kept his braided hair tied up in the city of Virata at that time."

sanskrit: sūdakarmaṇi ca śrāntaḥ virāṭasya mahānase bhīmasenena kaunteya yac ca tan mama pauruṣam
english: "And Bhimasena, O son of Kunti, exhausted in the work of a cook in Virata's great kitchen — that too speaks to my manhood."

sanskrit: evam eva sadā daṇḍaṃ kṣatriyāḥ kṣatriye dadhuḥ śreṇyāṃ kakṣyāṃ ca veṇyāṃ ca saṃyuge yaḥ palāyate
english: "In this very way have warriors always punished a warrior — in rank, in girdle, and in braid — who flees in battle."

sanskrit: na bhayād vāsudevasya na cāpi tava phalguna rājyaṃ pratipradāsyāmi yudhyasva sahakeśavaḥ
english: "Not out of fear of Vasudeva, nor of you, O Phalguna, will I surrender the kingdom — fight together with Keshava!"

sanskrit: na māyā hīndrajālaṃ vā kuhakā vā vibhīṣaṇī āttaśastrasya me yuddhe vahanti pratigarjanāḥ
english: "Illusions, conjuror's tricks, sorcery, or terrifying spectacles — these counter-roarings carry no weight against me when I stand weapons in hand in battle."

sanskrit: vāsudevasahasraṃ vā phalgunānāṃ śatāni vā āsādya mām amogheṣuṃ draviṣyanti diśo daśa
english: "A thousand Vasudevas or hundreds of Phalgunas — upon encountering me, whose arrows never miss, they will flee in all ten directions."

sanskrit: saṃyugaṃ gaccha bhīṣmeṇa bhindhi tvaṃ śirasā girim prataremaṃ mahāgādhaṃ bāhubhyāṃ puruṣodadhim
english: "Go meet Bhishma in battle — smash a mountain with your head! — cross this great unfathomable ocean of warriors with your own two arms!"

sanskrit: śāradvatamahīmānaṃ viviṃśatijhaṣākulam bṛhadbalasamuccālaṃ saumadattitimiṃgilam
english: "— whose heights are Sharadwata, teeming with Vivimshati as its fish, whose swells are Brihadbala, whose sea-monsters are Saumadatti —"

sanskrit: duḥśāsanaughaṃ śalaśalyamatsyaṃ; suṣeṇacitrāyudhanāganakram jayadrathādriṃ purumitragādhaṃ; durmarṣaṇodaṃ śakuniprapātam
english: "— whose floods are Duhshasana, whose fish are Shala and Shalya, whose crocodiles are Sushena and Chitrayudha, whose mountain is Jayadratha, whose depths are Purumitra, whose eddies are Durmarshana, whose cataracts are Shakuni —"

sanskrit: śastraugham akṣayyam atipravṛddhaṃ; yadāvagāhya śramanaṣṭacetāḥ bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ hatasarvabāndhavas; tadā manas te paritāpam eṣyati
english: "— the inexhaustible, ever-swelling torrent of weapons — when you plunge into it and emerge with mind exhausted and all kinsmen slain, then your mind will know torment."

sanskrit: tadā manas te tridivād ivāśucer; nivartatāṃ pārtha mahīpraśāsanāt rājyaṃ praśāstuṃ hi sudurlabhaṃ tvayā; bubhūṣatā svarga ivātapasvinā
english: "Then, O Partha, may your mind turn back from ruling the earth, as the impure are turned back from the third heaven — for to govern a kingdom is as impossible for you as reaching heaven is for one who has not practiced austerities."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca ulūkas tv arjunaṃ bhūyo yathoktaṃ vākyam abravīt āśīviṣam iva kruddhaṃ tudan vākyaśalākayā
english: Sanjaya said: Uluka again spoke to Arjuna the words as he had been told, stinging him with verbal darts like one goading an angry venomous serpent.

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā ruṣitāḥ pāṇḍavā bhṛśam prāg eva bhṛśasaṃkruddhāḥ kaitavyena pradharṣitāḥ
english: Hearing those words, the Pandavas were greatly enraged — already deeply angered as they had been, now further provoked by Uluka, son of Shakuni.

sanskrit: nāsaneṣv avatiṣṭhanta bāhūṃś caiva vicikṣipuḥ āśīviṣā iva kruddhā vīkṣāṃ cakruḥ parasparam
english: They could not remain seated; they flung their arms out and looked at one another like enraged venomous serpents.

sanskrit: avākśirā bhīmasenaḥ samudaikṣata keśavam netrābhyāṃ lohitāntābhyām āśīviṣa iva śvasan
english: Bhimasena, with head bent down, looked up at Keshava with eyes reddened at the corners, hissing like a venomous serpent.

sanskrit: ārtaṃ vātātmajaṃ dṛṣṭvā krodhenābhihataṃ bhṛśam utsmayann iva dāśārhaḥ kaitavyaṃ pratyabhāṣata
english: Seeing the son of the Wind-god distressed and deeply stricken by wrath, the descendant of Dasharha, smiling slightly, replied to Uluka, son of Shakuni.
